falsifier: The three pre-registered falsifiers, each with what this lane measured. (1) A fixture payload with a zoning facet holding R-1B and a not-onboarded atom yields status ok, declineReason envelope-unverified, figureWithheld true — PASS BY TEST, and by the meanest reading: F1 also pins district R-1B, setbackSource parcel-record, the record axes as setbacks, NO buildableAreaSqFt/Pct, facetCoverage.envelope true, and a disclosure naming the atom's DID `did:hauska:buildable-envelope:48309:103015` together with its own code `no-district-on-record` and the district; F1b pins that this envelope is exactly what fires the live derive, so the polygon's only source is allowed to run; the divergence test pins the same routing for the fixture's own `not-onboarded` and `unzoned` cases. (2) The same payload with the zoning facet absent yields no-zoning-stamp — PASS BY TEST, for a missing stamp, a null stamp and an empty stamp; the envelope is declined, nothing is drawn, no district is invented, facets.zoning is null, facetCoverage.envelope is false, and the disclosure is EXACTLY the atom's own live sentence; the divergence test shows all 13 declared cases declining with nothing drawn. (3) Reverting the fix fails a test — MEASURED, OBSERVED FAILING: with the three source files reverted to the parent commit 93f832b6 and the tests kept at HEAD, the two suites report 9 failures (6 + 3) — `expected 'declined' to be 'ok'`, `expected false to be true`, `expected 'no-zoning-stamp' to be 'envelope-unverified'`, `expected 'no-zoning-stamp' to be 'setback-rule-pending'`, `expected 'zoning-absent' to be 'no-zoning-stamp'`, plus two TypeErrors for the new exports that a revert cannot compile; restored from HEAD and re-run green at 138/138 with a clean tree (literal transcript in _inbox/2026-09-17_p303-not-onboarded-decline_falsifier3-revert.txt). NOT MEASURED by this lane: Waco 48309:103015 drawing on smartsite.cloud — that is the deployed-panel predicate and this dispatch forbids deploying.
contradicted: Three things this work puts in writing against the framing it was handed. (1) The dispatch's step-1 wording assumes the fix is about ONE branch that turns "no district"/"not onboarded" into `no-zoning-stamp`; measurement found the branch is guarded by ONE literal token (`absenceKind === "no-zoning-stamp"`) while the cohort the dispatch counts (153,775 "not onboarded" atoms) is named by OTHER strings — engine cascade codes and breadth-bake reason text — that until now fell to the adapter's generic `zoning-absent` fallback and never reached the `no-zoning-stamp` token at all. So there was not one producer but a class, and the honest fix had to name the class rather than patch one string. (2) A record-stamped district with an INCOMPLETE axis table must not be drawn: the dispatch's step 1 asks for the `envelope-unverified` branch "where ... a setback table exists", and the meanest reading of "a table exists" is not enough — front, side AND rear must all be served, or the drawn inset would invent the missing axes; that case declines with the file's existing `setback-rule-pending` token instead. (3) The lane ALSO changes a visible label for a sub-cohort: members whose only basis is a cascade code or a reason string and whose payload holds no district now print the card's "no zoning stamp here" absence label where they previously printed "no zoning here". Both are absent states and the fact sheet already collapses the two tokens into one branch, but it is a real difference and it is declared rather than discovered — and it follows from dispatch step 2, which requires the class to decline `no-zoning-stamp`.
missionPremise: An envelope atom whose basis is a stamp gap must not be read as "this parcel has no zoning". hauska-engine's own cascade module records that the cohort "targets every absence-zoning parcel county-wide, including parcels inside an incorporated city that IS zoned but simply has not been stamped yet ... the jurisdiction is zoned, only unonboarded" (packages/engine-core/src/property-reasoning/cascade-unzoned-envelope-decline.ts:25-31), and the contract's only zoning-absence kind, `no-zoning-stamp`, records that no zoning polygon stamped the parcel at bake time (hauska-atom-contract src/property/common.ts:59). Read together with the operator ruling of 2026-09-11 (Ruling B reversed for the POLYGON only: draw the modelled envelope wherever a district and a setback table exist, and let only the AREA wait — _decisions/2026-09-11_ruling_b_reversed_polygon_only.md) and P-249's branch (A-180: a buildable-area figure appears only when a VERIFIED envelope atom backs it), the conclusion is structural: a chain in the no-district class may not decide the envelope's status on its own when the payload already holds the district and the table the ruling asks for, and the figure must still stay withheld because the atom behind it is unverified. Population premise, CITED from the dispatch and NOT re-measured by this lane: the class is about 153,775 of the 490,185 six-county `no-buildable-area` atoms; P-255 owns that measurement.

Any branch that declines the facet deletes the drawing; that is why P-249 and P-303 are the same lever pulled twice.

2026-09-17: the shared fixture (envelope-verification.json, casesSha256 983bb015e65f3b4ab664ef174a408d0bf4baa60b904369e5ee1b1fe712a59e20, 13 cases) is read by predicates in three repos. Its divergence test in hauska-map asserted the verification predicate on every case but ran NO case through the adapter's decision tree, so the adapter could decline an atom the fixture declared unverified without a single test failing. Asserting a predicate over a fixture is not the same as asserting the ROUTE that consumes it.

When a fix is described as "one branch turns X into Y", enumerate the STRINGS that reach that branch before editing it: here the literal guard was `absenceKind === "no-zoning-stamp"` (one wire token) while the cohort the dispatch counted was named by two engine cascade codes and two breadth-bake reason strings that fell to a generic fallback and never reached the token at all. The class had to be named (and its members' genuine-absence verdicts declared) before the branch could be safely widened.

A falsifier that asks "reverting the fix fails a test" needs the SOURCE reverted and the TESTS kept — `git stash` on a committed branch silently does nothing ('No local changes to save') and the run then passes green against the fixed code. Use `git checkout <parent> -- <source files>`, run, then `git checkout HEAD -- <source files>`.

Do not call "a setback table exists" a predicate until it defines which axes: an inset needs front, side and rear, so a partial row must decline rather than have the missing axes invented for it. The cheap version of this lane would have drawn a fabricated inset on any district stamp.

Do not try to fix this in the record overlay (pe-property-atoms.ts applyRecordPatch): it runs AFTER the adapter has already decided the envelope, so an overlay can re-label or re-stamp a declined envelope but cannot make the live derive fire. The status has to be decided where the envelope is built.

Do not look for the panel's draw logic in the client. InspectCard resolves one sealed fact sheet and issues no envelope lookup of its own; the live derive is gated inside the sheet's resolver on the BAKED facet status (live-envelope-augment.ts, called from fact-sheet-resolver.ts). Reasoning from the card's "baked first, live fallback" header (P-249's dead end) still leads to the wrong file.

The deployed-panel proof: /api/spine/property-atoms/48309%3A103015/facets must return envelope.status "ok" with geometry drawn and no area figure after PR 411 deploys; capture the build identity by asset existence (never Age:) from a fresh browser context, and re-check the control case.

The class predicate's substring leg means a NEW wording for this cohort in hauska-engine would silently fall out of the class and be declined again. Whoever coins one should extend NO_DISTRICT_DECLINE_SOURCES; the inventory test fails if a member is added without a verdict.

P-257 (decline wording) and P-255 (population) are adjacent: the tokens this lane reuses (`envelope-unverified` with status "ok", `setback-rule-pending` with a district) are now load-bearing and should not be re-worded without re-running P-303's suites.
